events.summary: AAOI closed at $115.59, up 7.71% (from $107.32), on 1.52x its normal 20-day volume, with no company announcement and no SEC filing. It followed an +8.1% AAOI gain on Thursday 2026-10-01, a day when Coherent rose 10% (new PhotonLink platform plus a Bernstein 'outperform' initiation) and Lumentum rose 9%.
events.why_it_matters: The move tells Santi about the sector mood, not about AOI's business. Our attribution model puts 1.15 points down to the market, 2.6 points to the chip/optics industry and 3.96 points to AAOI itself, and calls the company part 'within its normal day-to-day noise' (z-score 0.5). AAOI usually moves about 7.9% a day on its own, so a 7.7% day is ordinary for this stock.

events.summary: Q2 2026: record revenue of $191.9M (up 86.4% from $103.0M a year earlier; fifth record quarter in a row). Data center revenue $107.7M (56.1% of sales, up 140.4%); CATV (cable TV) $80.6M (42.0%). Non-GAAP net income $5.5M ($0.06 per share), first non-GAAP profit after losses; GAAP net loss $22.8M. events.summary: AOI signed a new 'at-the-market' (ATM) agreement with Raymond James and Needham to sell up to $600M of new shares over time (agents earn 2%), filed with a 424B5 prospectus. It is the third equity program of 2026: the first ($250M, upsized to $500M) sold about 4.8M shares at an average $103.51 for about $490M net, completed 2026-04-02; a second $600M program was signed 2026-05-14. Shares outstanding rose from 74.998M (2025-12-31) to 84.386M (2026-06-30). The stock fell 13.8% on Monday 2026-08-24.
events.why_it_matters: Each new share sold makes every existing share a slightly smaller slice of the company (dilution). It funds the factory build-out, but repeated raises are a recurring drag on the share price and on per-share profit.

events.summary: AOI is spending heavily to build factories for 800G/1.6T transceivers: construction started on two Pearland, Texas properties adding nearly 400,000 sq ft (2026-07-14); two more Houston buildings leased for 10 years (2026-08-31, completion about 16 months out); a 153,928 sq ft Houston building bought for $26.8M cash (2026-09-04); and a 38,312 square-metre factory leased in Ningbo, China for 10 years from 2026-09-16 (rent RMB 6.9M a year). Management targets capacity of about 650,000 800G/1.6T units per month by end-2026, versus total capacity 'approaching 200,000 units per month' at Q2.
events.why_it_matters: The bull case depends on AOI turning this new capacity into shipped, paid-for product; the cost of building it is why the company keeps selling shares.

why_chain.text: AAOI rose 7.71% on Friday 2026-10-02 to $115.59, after +8.1% on Thursday; up 13.99% for the week.

About half the day's move came from the market (+1.15 pts) and the chip/optics industry (+2.6 pts); the AAOI-only part (+3.96 pts) is within its normal daily noise. Over the week, the industry explains more than the company (+8.16 vs +6.18 pts).
There was no AOI press release, SEC filing or analyst action on 2026-10-02; 24/7 Wall St. states no company announcement came with the move.

Optical peers rose together (Lumentum +3%, Coherent +4%, SOXX +3% on Oct 2), continuing an Oct 1 rally sparked by Coherent's PhotonLink AI data-center optics platform and Bernstein starting Coherent at outperform.

Investors bought the whole AI-optics group because they expect big cloud companies to keep spending heavily on fibre links between AI chips; AAOI, a smaller and loss-making supplier, swings much more than its peers on the same news (model: 1.95x the industry's excess move, 1-year beta 4.25).

products.name: 800G and 1.6T optical transceivers (Data Center segment)
products.what_it_is: Small plug-in modules that turn electrical signals into laser light and back, so AI servers and network switches can talk over fibre-optic cable at 800 or 1,600 gigabits per second.
products.analogy: A translator at each end of a phone line: the switch speaks 'electricity', the fibre speaks 'light', and the transceiver converts between them, billions of times a second.
products.buyers: Large cloud/AI data-center operators (hyperscalers). AOI does not name them in releases; the 10-Q discloses a warrant issued in March 2025 to a wholly owned subsidiary of Amazon, a customer-incentive arrangement.
products.how_it_works: AOI makes its own laser chips (vertical integration) and assembles them into modules in Texas, Taiwan and China; each AI cluster needs many transceivers per GPU, so faster AI build-outs mean more modules.
products.sales: Data Center segment revenue $107.7M in Q2 2026 (56.1% of total, up 140.4% year on year) per 10-Q. Product-level: 800G revenue about $12.8M in Q2 (11.9% of data-center revenue), more than doubled sequentially, with management expecting nearly 5x sequential growth in Q3 (Zacks summary of the call; tier 3, not checked against transcript). 1.6T: first volume order of more than $200M from a hyperscaler, shipping Q3-Q4 2026 (tier 3 reports, primary release not retrieved).
products.stage: 800G ramping in volume; 1.6T first volume order, shipments scheduled for Q3-Q4 2026
products.size_for_company: Already the largest segment: 56% of Q2 revenue. Q3 guidance of $255M-$290M implies large further data-center growth (inference).
products.competition: Coherent, Lumentum, and large Chinese makers (e.g. Innolight, Eoptolink; named from general industry knowledge, not from a source fetched today).
products.why_investors_care: This is the AI growth engine and the reason the stock is up 231% this year; it is also where capacity and customer concentration risk sit.
products.watch_next: Q3 data-center revenue and 800G/1.6T unit commentary on ~2026-11-05; progress toward ~650,000 units/month capacity by end-2026.

products.name: 1.8GHz CATV amplifiers and QuantumLink software (CATV segment)
products.what_it_is: Signal boosters placed along cable-TV/broadband coaxial lines, upgraded to carry 1.8 GHz of spectrum (DOCSIS 4.0) for faster home internet, plus remote-management software.
products.analogy: Booster pumps along a water main; the upgrade lets the pipe carry far more water, and the software lets the utility watch every pump from headquarters.
products.buyers: Cable operators; Spectrum (Charter) is a named customer for both the connected 1.8GHz amplifiers and the QuantumLink software (2026-06-10). The 10-Q shows distributor Digicomm owing $211.0M of AOI's $314.0M receivables.
products.how_it_works: Operators replace older amplifiers across their networks; AOI sells the hardware and now the control software.
products.sales: CATV segment revenue $80.6M in Q2 2026 (42.0% of total, up 43.8% year on year). More than 1 million 1.8GHz amplifiers shipped as of 2026-09-24.
products.stage: shipping in volume; 3.0GHz next-generation shown only as a concept demo (2026-09-24)
products.size_for_company: About 42% of Q2 revenue; the steadier second leg of the business.
products.why_investors_care: Provides revenue that does not depend on AI spending, but is concentrated in a few cable customers via one distributor.
products.watch_next: CATV revenue trend in Q3; Digicomm receivable balance in the Q3 10-Q.
